Class DtlsConfig

java.lang.Object
com.quietterminal.neon.core.DtlsConfig
public final class DtlsConfig extends Object
Factory methods for constructing SSLContext instances configured for DTLS.

The relay holds the server certificate and private key; hosts and clients trust that certificate. Typical setup:

  • Relay: fromKeyStore(KeyStore, char[]) — has certificate + key
  • Host / Client: withTrustStore(KeyStore) — trusts the relay certificate
  • Development / testing: insecureTrustAll() — accepts any certificate

Pass the returned SSLContext to NeonConfig.Builder.sslContext(SSLContext). When sslContext is set on a NeonConfig, all components using that config will communicate over DTLS.

  • Method Details

    • fromKeyStore

      public static SSLContext fromKeyStore(KeyStore keyStore, char[] keyPassword) throws Exception
      Creates a server-side SSLContext backed by the given key store. Use this on the relay, which holds the server certificate and private key.
      Parameters:
      keyStore - key store containing the certificate chain and private key
      keyPassword - password protecting the private key entry
      Returns:
      configured DTLS SSLContext
      Throws:
      Exception - if the context cannot be initialised

    • withTrustStore

      public static SSLContext withTrustStore(KeyStore trustStore) throws Exception
      Creates a client-side SSLContext that trusts certificates in the given trust store. Use this on hosts and clients connecting to a relay whose certificate is in trustStore.
      Parameters:
      trustStore - key store containing the trusted relay certificate(s)
      Returns:
      configured DTLS SSLContext
      Throws:
      Exception - if the context cannot be initialised

    • insecureTrustAll

      public static SSLContext insecureTrustAll() throws Exception
      Creates a SSLContext that accepts any server certificate without validation.

      Never use this in production. For local development and integration tests only.

      Returns:
      an insecure DTLS SSLContext
      Throws:
      Exception - if the context cannot be initialised
